{{nihongo|'''Eda Shrine'''|江田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]].

'''Eda Shrine''' (えだじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Awagihara-chō|ja|阿波岐原町|qid=Q132132174}} (Awagihara-chō), {{ill|Miyazaki (city)|Q204308|qid=Q204308}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300|qid=Q130300}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and its former shrine rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
'''Main enshrined deity'''
* '''{{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto}}''' (いざなぎのみこと)

'''Associated enshrined deity'''
* {{ill|Izanami|ar|إزانامي|az|İzanami|bcl|Izanami|bs|Izanami|ca|Izanami|da|Izanami|el|Ιζανάμι|eo|Izanami|es|Izanami|fa|ایزانامی|fi|Izanami|fr|Izanami|he|איזאנמי|hr|Izanami|hu|Izanami|hy|Իզանամի|id|Izanami|it|Izanami|ja|イザナミ|ko|이자나미|mk|Изанами|mni|ꯏꯓꯥꯅꯥꯃꯤ|pt|Izanami|rsk|Изанами|ru|Идзанами|simple|Izanami|sl|Izanami|sr|Изанами|sv|Izanami|ta|இசநமி|th|อิซานามิ|tl|Izanami|tr|Izanami|uk|Ідзанамі|zh|伊邪那美|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto}} (いざなみのみこと) – Enshrined additionally in {{ill|Juei|fa|جوئی|fr|Ère Juei|ia|Juei|id|Juei|ja|寿永|ko|주에이|ru|Дзюэй|simple|Juei|sr|Џуеи|tr|Juei|zh|壽永|zh_yue|壽永|qid=Q598057}} 2 ({{ill|1183|ab|1183|af|1183|als|1183|am|1183 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1183|ar|1183|ary|1183|ast|1183|avk|1183|az|1183|azb|۱۱۸۳ (میلادی)|bcl|1183|be|1183|be_x_old|1183|bg|1183|bn|১১৮৩|bpy|মারি ১১৮৩|br|1183|bs|1183.|ca|1183|cdo|1183 nièng|ceb|1183|ckb|١١٨٣|crh|1183|cs|1183|cv|1183|cy|1183|da|1183|de|1183|diq|1183|el|1183|eml|1183|eo|1183|es|1183|et|1183|eu|1183|fa|۱۱۸۳ (میلادی)|fi|1183|fo|1183|fr|1183|frr|1183|fy|1183|ga|1183|gan|1183年|gcr|1183|gd|1183|gl|1183|he|1183|hi|११८३|hr|1183.|ht|1183 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1183|hy|1183|id|1183|ilo|1183|io|1183|is|1183|it|1183|ja|1183年|jv|1183|ka|1183|kaa|1183|kk|1183 жыл|ko|1183년|la|1183|lb|1183|lij|1183|lmo|1183|lt|1183 m.|lv|1183. gads|map_bms|1183|mdf|1183|mg|1183|mhr|1183|mi|1183|min|1183|mk|1183|mr|इ.स. ११८३|mrj|1183 и|ms|1183|mzn|۱۱۸۳|nah|1183|nap|1183|nds|1183|new|सन् ११८३|nl|1183|nn|1183|no|1183|nrm|1183|nso|1183|oc|1183|or|୧୧୮୩|os|1183-æм аз|pl|1183|pnb|1183|pt|1183|qu|1183|ro|1183|ru|1183 год|rue|1183|sa|११८३|sc|1183|scn|1183|sd|1183ع|se|1183|sh|1183.|shn|1183|simple|1183|sk|1183|sl|1183|smn|1183|sq|1183|sr|1183|su|1183|sv|1183|sw|1183|tg|Соли 1183|th|พ.ศ. 1726|tk|1183|tl|1183|tly|1183|tr|1183|tt|1183 ел|uk|1183|ur|1183ء|uz|1183|vec|1183|vi|1183|war|1183|wuu|1183年|xmf|1183|zea|1183|zh|1183年|zh_min_nan|1183 nî|zh_yue|1183年|qid=Q19723}}).

These two deities are collectively called “Yabo Nihashira Daimyōjin” (産母二柱大明神), and are also affectionately referred to by local people as “Yabo-sama.”

=== History ===
=== Mythology ===
According to the '{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}' and '{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}', Izanagi-no-Mikoto returned from {{ill|Yomi|ar|يومي|de|Yomi|es|Yomi|fa|یومی|fr|Yomi (mythologie)|id|Yomi|it|Yomi|ja|黄泉|no|Yomi|pl|Yomi|pt|Yomi|ru|Ёми|simple|Yomi|th|โยมิ|tr|Yomi|uk|Йомі|ur|یومی|qid=Q1142558}} and performed a {{ill|Misogi|ar|ميسوجي|az|Misoqi|cs|Misogi|da|Misogi|de|Misogi|el|Μισόγκι|es|Misogi|fa|میسوگی|fr|Misogi|id|Misogi|it|Misogi|ja|禊|ko|미소기|te|మిసోగి|tr|Misogi|vi|Misogi|zh|禊 (日本)|qid=Q1936265}} purification ritual. Regarding the location where the misogi was performed, the 'Kojiki' records it as “Awagihara of the small inlet of Tachibana in Hyūga of Tsukushi,” while the 'Nihon Shoki' records it as “Awagihara (Aki-bara) of the small inlet of Tachibana in Hyūga of Tsukushi.” This Awagihara / Aki-bara is traditionally identified as the present site. This place name is also recited at the beginning of the {{ill|Norito|de|Norito|es|Norito|fa|نوریتو|fr|Norito|gl|Norito|id|Norito|it|Norito|ja|祝詞|pl|Norito|ru|Норито|te|నోరిటో|tr|Norito|uk|Норіто|zh|祝詞|qid=Q1760119}} chanted at shrines throughout Japan: “Kakemaku mo kashikoki Izanagi no Ōkami, Tsukushi no Hyūga no Tachibana no Odo no Awagihara ni misogi-harae tamai shi toki ni…”. For this reason, the area is regarded as “the birthplace of purification rituals.”<ref>{{Cite web|ja|url= http://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/shinwanofurusato/sp/img/pamph/pdf/01.pdf |title= Hyūga Mythology Journey |website= Miyazaki Prefecture |accessdate= 2021-11-07 }}</ref>

The nearby “Misogi Pond” is said to be the place where Izanagi-no-Mikoto performed the purification. It was once an inlet, but later reclaimed and named “Eda.”<ref name="説明板"/> Based on the above mythology, the area is also believed to be the birthplace of Izanagi’s children {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amaterasu}}, {{ill|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|ar|تسوكويومي|az|Tsukuyomi|bcl|Tsukuyomi|ca|Tsukuyomi|cs|Cukujomi|da|Tsuki-yomi|de|Tsukuyomi|el|Τσουκουγιόμι|eo|Cukujomi|es|Tsukuyomi|eu|Tsukuyomi|fa|تسوکویومی|fi|Tsukuyomi|fr|Tsukuyomi|hr|Tsukuyomi|hu|Cukujomi|hy|Ցուկույոմի-նո-Միկոտո|id|Tsukuyomi|it|Tsukuyomi|ja|ツクヨミ|ko|츠쿠요미|mk|Цукујоми|mni|ꯁꯨꯀꯨꯌꯣꯃꯤ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|no|Tsukuyomi|pl|Tsukuyomi|pt|Tsukuyomi|rsk|Цукуйоми|ru|Цукиёми|sh|Tsukuyomi|simple|Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto|sl|Cukijomi|sr|Цукујоми|su|Tsukuyomi|sv|Tsukuyomi|ta|சுக்குயோமி|th|สึกูโยมิ|tr|Tsukuyomi no Mikoto|uk|Цукуйомі|vi|Tsukuyomi|zh|月讀|zh_min_nan|Tukuyomi|qid=Q595520|lt=Tsukuyomi}}, and {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|Q272993|qid=Q272993}}—collectively known as the {{ill|Three Noble Children|fr|Trois Enfants Nobles|ja|三貴子|ko|삼귀자|pl|Troje Szlachetnych Dzieci|ru|Михасира-но-удзу-но мико|vi|Mikiko|zh|三貴子|zh_yue|三貴子|qid=Q4702904}}—as well as the {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|de|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|it|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|ja|住吉三神|mni|ꯁꯨꯃꯤꯌꯣꯁꯤ ꯁꯟꯖꯤꯟ|my|ဆုမိရောရှိနတ်သုံးပါး|pl|Sumiyoshi Sanjin|simple|Sumiyoshi sanjin|zh|住吉三神|qid=Q1114013}}.<ref name="説明板"/>

Numerous ancient settlement remains are found around the shrine, including the representative Aoki Site dating to the early {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}} (about 2,400 years ago). From Aoki No. 1 Tumulus, an early {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|Q11268718|qid=Q11268718}} keyhole-shaped burial mound dating to the late 3rd century, the largest wooden burial chamber and coffin remains in Japan have been discovered.

=== Historical overview ===
The earliest mention in national histories appears in the '{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}', under the entry for the 1st day of the 8th month of {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} 4 ({{ill|837|ab|837|af|837|als|837|am|837 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|837|ar|837|ary|837|ast|837|avk|837|az|837|azb|۸۳۷ (میلادی)|bcl|837|be|837|be_x_old|837|bg|837|bn|৮৩৭|bpy|মারি ৮৩৭|br|837|bs|837.|ca|837|cdo|837 nièng|ceb|837|ckb|٨٣٧|crh|837|cs|837|csb|837|cv|837|cy|837|da|837|de|837|el|837|eml|837|eo|837|es|837|et|837|eu|837|fa|۸۳۷ (میلادی)|fi|837|fo|837|fr|837|frr|837|fy|837|ga|837|gan|837年|gd|837|gl|837|he|837|hi|837|hr|837.|ht|837 (almanak jilyen)|hu|837|hy|837|id|837|ilo|837|io|837|it|837|ja|837年|jv|837|ka|837|kaa|837|kk|837 жыл|ko|837년|la|837|lb|837|lij|837|lmo|837|lt|837 m.|lv|837. gads|map_bms|837|mdf|837|mg|837|mhr|837|mk|837|mr|इ.स. ८३७|mrj|837 и|ms|837|mzn|۸۳۷|nah|837|nap|837|nds|837|new|सन् ८३७|nl|837|nn|837|no|837|nrm|837|nso|837|oc|837|or|୮୩୭|os|837-æм аз|pl|837|pnb|837|pt|837|qu|837|ro|837|ru|837 год|rue|837|sa|८३७|sah|837|scn|837|sd|837ع|se|837|sh|837.|shn|837|si|837|sk|837|sl|837|smn|837|sq|837|sr|837|su|837|sv|837|sw|837|tg|Соли 837|th|พ.ศ. 1380|tk|837|tl|837|tly|837|tr|837|tt|837 ел|uk|837|ur|837ء|uz|837|vec|837|vi|837|vls|837|war|837|wuu|837年|xmf|837|zh|837年|zh_min_nan|837 nî|zh_yue|837年|qid=Q25093}}): “Tsuno Shrine of Koyu District, Hyūga Province; Tsuma Shrine; '''Eda Shrine''' of Miyazaki District; Kirishima Mine Shrine of Morokata District—all placed among the official shrines.” In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, it is listed as “Eda Shrine” in Miyazaki District of Hyūga Province, and classified as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}. The '{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}' records an “Eda Village” in Miyazaki District, and Sue ware from around the 10th century has been excavated from the precincts, suggesting that the shrine still stands on its original site since its founding.<ref name="地名"/>

By {{ill|Tenroku|de|Tenroku|fa|تنروکو|fr|Ère Tenroku|ia|Tenroku|id|Tenroku|ja|天禄|ko|덴로쿠|ru|Тэнроку|simple|Tenroku|sr|Тенроку|tr|Tenroku|uk|Тенроку|zh|天祿 (日本)|zh_yue|天祿 (日本)|qid=Q1327229}} 1 ({{ill|970|Q24047|qid=Q24047}}), its {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} had risen to the highest level of {{ill|Senior First Rank|Q11123258|qid=Q11123258}}, and it is said to have once flourished with a magnificent shrine building bearing the chrysanthemum crest. In the medieval period it belonged to {{ill|Naka district|Q10978107|qid=Q10978107}}, and is mentioned in Kyoto’s “Kiyotaki Shrine Kanjin Jinmyōchō” as well as the “Kaidanin Official Shrine Register” of {{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} 11 ({{ill|1479|Q6620|qid=Q6620}}), indicating that it was regarded as one of the representative shrines of Hyūga Province.<ref name="地名"/> During the Edo period, it was under shogunal land, the {{ill|Itō clan|Q2975280|qid=Q2975280}}, and the {{ill|Obi Domain|Q8192240|qid=Q8192240}} as entrusted territory.

However, after losing its buildings to the great tsunami caused by the {{ill|Kanbun (era)|Q1146228|qid=Q1146228}} 2 ({{ill|1662|Q7574|qid=Q7574}}) {{ill|1662 Hyūga-nada earthquake|Q11430459|qid=Q11430459}}, the shrine declined and came to be treated as the tutelary shrine of a single village.<ref name="地名"/> It is also said that many valuable historical artifacts were lost to the tsunami. In the early {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963}}, the Shinto scholar {{ill|Tachibana Mitsuyoshi|Q11544184|qid=Q11544184}} wrote in his 'Shokoku Ichinomiya Junpaiki': “I visited the shrine of Eda, then worshiped at Sumiyoshi of Awagihara. When I inquired, I was told that the pine trees of Sumiyoshi are the pine groves of Awagihara. On this seashore, Izanagi-no-Mikoto performed his purification.”

=== Sacred pond ===
[[File:Eda-jinja (Miyazaki) Miike-1.JPG|thumb|200px|right|Sacred Pond (Misogi Pond)]]
The pond where Izanagi-no-Mikoto is said to have performed the misogi is located northeast of the shrine ({{Coord|31|57|50.19|N|131|28|02.92|E|region:JP-45_type:landmark|name=Sacred Pond (Misogi Pond)}}), and is called “Miike” or “Misogi Pond.”<ref>The name of the pond is based on the on-site explanatory sign.</ref>
<gallery>
File:Misogi goten.JPG|Misogi Hall
</gallery>

=== Festivals ===
* Kinen-sai (February 17)<ref>Festival information based on on-site explanatory sign.</ref>
* Ōharae-sai (June 30)
*: As a special ritual, Chinowa kuguri is performed.<ref name="説明板">On-site explanatory sign.</ref> In the past, it was customary to perform a beach purification at the shore on the previous night.<ref name="地名">“Place Names of Miyazaki Prefecture,” entry on Eda Shrine.</ref> On the day of the ritual, after the mikoshi procession, priests, parishioners, and worshippers pass through the chinowa in that order.<ref name="地名"/>
* Grand Annual Festival (November 22)
* Niiname-sai (November 23)

At the Spring Shaden Festival and the Autumn Grand Festival, “Eda Kagura” is dedicated. The history of this kagura is ancient, and kagura masks inscribed with the year Keichō 17 still remain.
